1. Executive Summary

The Future of PMM is an internal learning platform for SAP Product Marketing serving ~170 registered users. The site includes a 12-unit curriculum, interactive assessments, AI-powered labs, and a weekly newsletter system.

Migration Goal: Move from Netlify + Supabase to SAP-managed infrastructure on Business Technology Platform (BTP), leveraging SAP Identity Authentication Service (IAS) for SSO.

3. Database Schema

3.1 Core Tables

-- User profiles (linked to Auth)
CREATE TABLE profiles (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  first_name TEXT,
  last_name TEXT,
  company TEXT DEFAULT 'SAP',
  role TEXT,
  team TEXT,
  newsletter_opt_in BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- Quiz scores for curriculum units
CREATE TABLE quiz_scores (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID REFERENCES profiles(id),
  chapter TEXT NOT NULL,  -- 'unit-01', 'unit-02', etc.
  score INTEGER NOT NULL,
  total INTEGER NOT NULL,
  percentage INTEGER NOT NULL,
  completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- Assessment results (10x Scorecard, Cognitive Style)
CREATE TABLE assessment_results (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID REFERENCES profiles(id),
  assessment_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  result_key TEXT,
  result_name TEXT,
  result_data JSONB,
  completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- Survey/feedback responses
CREATE TABLE survey_responses (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  email TEXT,
  value_rating INTEGER,
  nps INTEGER,
  improvements TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

6. Authentication Architecture

6.1 Current Flow (Magic Link)

  1. User enters SAP email on login page
  2. System sends magic link via Resend
  3. User clicks link → JWT token generated
  4. Token stored in localStorage (7-day expiry)
  5. Token validated on each protected page

6.2 SAP Alternative: SAP Identity Authentication Service (IAS)

Benefits of SAP IAS:
  • Single sign-on with existing SAP credentials
  • Automatic user provisioning from SAP directory
  • Automatic role/team mapping from SAP HR data
  • Audit logging for compliance
  • No separate password management
Note: Current system restricts to @sap.com email addresses only. SAP IAS would eliminate the need for separate account creation.

8. Migration Steps

  1. Phase 1: Infrastructure Setup
    Provision SAP HANA Cloud or PostgreSQL on BTP. Set up SAP IAS for authentication. Configure Cloud Foundry runtime for serverless functions.
  2. Phase 2: Database Migration
    Export data from Supabase (CSV/JSON). Create tables in SAP database. Import profiles, quiz scores, progress data. Verify data integrity.
  3. Phase 3: Authentication Migration
    Configure SAP IAS integration. Map existing users to SAP directory. Update frontend auth code. Test SSO flow.
  4. Phase 4: Function Migration
    Port Netlify Functions to SAP BTP runtime. Update environment variables. Configure AI service access (if approved). Update API endpoints.
  5. Phase 5: DNS & Go-Live
    Configure SAP CDN/hosting. Update DNS records. SSL certificate provisioning. Cutover with minimal downtime.

9.2 Recommendation

The AI labs are valuable but not critical to core learning. Suggest:
  • Core curriculum (Units 1-12) works without AI
  • Labs marked as "AI-powered" with fallback content
  • AI access added post-migration if/when approved
